title: Built a freqtrade-based momentum-trend bot and documented its REAL edge (including the ugly parts)
author: SubjectPenalty1352
selftext:
Backtested 46 Binance pairs, 4h, 2021–2026: +1045%, PF 2.79, max DD 16.5%, OOS PF 4.83.

Ran freqtrade lookahead-analysis → has\_bias = No.

Full transparency: headline carried by one ZEC 17x rally. Strip it out → PF \~1.9 full period, NEGATIVE last 12 months. Published honestly in README.

One-command Docker, dry-run by default. Code + docs + honest methodology:

[https://github.com/MakimaAI/TrendFlow](https://github.com/MakimaAI/TrendFlow)

How do others handle single-trade dependence in trend strategies — red flag or just trend-following nature?

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Respect the transparency, most people hide that kind of stuff. But a 17x ZEC rally carrying your headline numbers is a red flag, not just 'trend-following nature.' Strip that out and you're at PF 1.9 with negative last 12 months - that's a regime-dependent strategy, not an edge. The lookahead analysis coming back clean is good, but it doesn't solve the concentration problem. Real trend following accepts that a few trades carry the book, but you need enough independent opportunities for that to work statistically. One pair doing all the work means your strategy is really 'one market did something once.' I'd want to see how it handles correlated drawdowns across the 46 pairs before trusting the OOS numbers.

replies.author: SubjectPenalty1352
replies.body:
You're right, and I appreciate you taking the time to actually read it. Most of this criticism is fair, and some of it I already knew — I just didn't hide it.

Let me be precise, because you deserve real numbers, not marketing.

You're correct on the headline:

\- The +1045% headline is carried by one single trade: ZEC 2025, a \~13.75x move held for 60 days. That one trade is \~69% of the net profit.

\- Remove ZEC and the full-period result is a profit factor of about 1.9, and negative over the last 12 months on that subset. That's exactly what I documented.

Where I think you're also right about the nature of the problem:

\- It's not really trend-following. A real trend-following book relies on many independent, loosely-correlated opportunities so the statistics work out. Here, one pair did all the work. That's not an edge — that's one market did something once and the strategy happened to be in it.

\- I already knew this before your comment. You can see it in docs/v8-gerceklik-analizi.md, which I published, and which says explicitly that ZEC is a real jackpot, not an edge, and shows 2021–2024 without ZEC was +139%, profit factor 1.68, CAGR 27% — a real but modest edge. And the ZEC-less out-of-sample was -23.8%. I didn't hide any of it.

Where I'd push back, honestly:

\- The strategy was not just one pair over the whole period. I ran it across 46 pairs, and did a per-coin analysis (docs/v8-percoin-analizi.md). Result: roughly 45-50% of individual coins have a profit factor above 1 — the edge is real but it's not diversified in the way you'd want. A handful carry it. You're right that this is the weak point.

\- Lookahead is clean (has\_bias = No) — which you acknowledged. But I agree that doesn't solve concentration. I never claimed it did.

On your specific ask, correlated drawdowns across 46 pairs:

\- I did test this indirectly. The different-universe test (docs/v8-farkli-evren-testi.md) showed the 36-coin extended universe came out -25.4%, profit factor 0.88. So outside the core 46, the edge largely doesn't hold, and it dilutes when combined. That's strong evidence the edge is universe-specific, and the drawdown correlation across the book is higher than a healthy trend-following book would want.

\- I also explicitly tried to kill the ZEC dependency and failed. Trailing stop (-53% vs baseline), ATR stop (-77%), loose momentum (profit factor 1.89), etc. Several "fixes" made it worse or overstated. The time-based exit is the only thing that consistently captures these moves, and its own win rate is 100% on that subset — which again points to concentration, not robustness.

So, summarizing honestly:

\- This is a regime-dependent, concentration-heavy strategy. A few big trend windows carry it. In a strong-trend regime (2025 ZEC) it looks great; in chop or a ZEC-less window it's modest-to-negative.

\- I am NOT claiming this is a robust, diversified edge. It isn't. It's an honest, documented, backtested momentum-trend strategy where one outlier inflates the optics.

\- I published the reality check precisely because I don't want anyone to read the headline +1045% and deploy real money into it. The README says so directly.
